The root cause is visible: a module-level `_used_codes` set records every applied code and `is_eligible` rejects any code in it. Let me confirm with the test run.
The test results confirm the diagnosis. Some failures are a side effect of the shared state (e.g. `FLAT5` and `SAVE10` are already in `_used_codes` from earlier tests in the same process).

args.root_cause: `library/discounts.py` keeps a module-level set `_used_codes` that is never cleared. `apply_discount` adds `discount.code` to this set every time a discount is applied, and `is_eligible` returns False for any code already in the set. So a multi-use code like SAVE10 applies once per process lifetime; every later order is silently skipped (the subtotal is returned unchanged). This matches the report: the first order works, later orders don't, and restarting the service (which clears the set) gives one more success. The code was never deactivated, so the cause is this process-global "used" tracking, not admin config. The test suite also shows this: `test_discount_object_is_reusable_across_separate_orders` fails, and other discount tests fail because codes applied in earlier tests remain in `_used_codes` (test pollution from the same state).
